shots.narration: Five operating problems. First, how CIB originates an IPO and how Private Banking onboards founders and executives on a consent basis. Second, how a new client, a next-generation member or a spouse completes a first investment. Third, where the family's money actually goes twelve months after a death. Fourth, how the Private Bank is actually performing — AUM, revenue, client commission, gross margin, net margin and cost-to-income, with the formulas on one dashboard. Fifth, why a trade fails — client, market, RM, operations or IT — and how the RM turns that attribution into knowledge and a better client conversation.

shots.narration: This is the wealth-event pipeline. We do not look only at IPOs. We include IPOs, H-share listings, secondary sell-downs, M&A and employee ownership trusts in one pipeline. Each row carries the company, exchange, stage, expected timing, CIB coverage, founder and management holdings, estimated wealth, Private Banking status and the responsible relationship manager. The point is not to obtain a list of names. The point is to put the event, client consent, Chinese Wall clearance and Private Banking readiness on one page. The public cases — DeepSeek, Mindray, Lens Technology, Riverford and Unruly — illustrate the structure only. They are not client relationships.

shots.narration: This is family onboarding. A private-banking client is not a single client ID. It is a family graph: principal, spouse, adult children, minor children, trustees, lawyers and the family office. Each person has a role, consent status, goals and entitlements. Three points are critical. A parent cannot consent on behalf of an adult child. A minor's authority comes from guardianship or a trust. A spouse's authority comes from their own consent or a valid legal instrument. The permission model below is the hard system boundary that prevents "the parent decides everything".

shots.narration: The portfolio shows time, value and outcome in one table: one trust ran twenty-three years and closed on 30 August 2026; one benchmark paid fifteen days after the grant.

This is the timeline of one case. The sequence matters. At T+0 the death is notified and the power of attorney ends automatically. At T+1 the family makes contact, but the executor has not yet been granted probate. At T+7 funeral and urgent expenses arise. At T+30 probate is filed. At T+60 the grant is issued. At T+90 the estate account and distributions are handled. At T+365 the outcome is reviewed. The bank cannot treat family consensus as authority, and cannot transfer assets to the family before the grant. This page puts the legal action, bank action and evidence on one timeline.

shots.narration: This is failure detail. ORD-1002: UK creator family, London, order at 16:44, after the close. Primary cause: market closed. Contributing cause: the market-hours check was missed; it is not an IT failure. The page separates cause, contributing cause, owner and evidence. The RM explains what happened, why, who is affected, what happens next, and what to check next time. Recovery: rebook next session, confirm with the client, log evidence. IT-caused failures are tagged separately, so they can be found and fixed. That explanation is how a failure becomes trust.
